headline: AI investment scam reports up nearly 400%, FCA warns: check the firm first
summary: Reports of investment fraud that mention suspected AI rose from 193 to 956 in a year, the Financial Conduct Authority says. Before you invest, look the firm up on its Firm Checker.
body: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published new figures on 26 November. Reports of investment fraud to Report Fraud that mention suspected use of AI rose from 193 in 2024/25 to 956 in 2025/26, a rise of nearly 400%. Investment fraud victims lost an average of £28,188 in 2025/26.

A third of UK adults (33%) say they saw an investment promotion in the past year that they believed used AI, such as a faked video or voice. Almost two thirds (62%) think they could spot an AI investment scam, yet under half (49%) think they could tell if a video or voice of a well-known person was AI-generated or altered. Martin Lewis came up most often among the famous faces people saw in fake promotions.

Under-35s feel the most confident and see the most of these adverts. Only 38% of them would check a firm is authorised before investing, against 73% of over-65s. “AI makes creating online scams easier and harder for people to identify,” says Sheree Howard, the FCA’s executive director of authorisations. The survey, by Kantar, asked 2,558 people in the UK aged 16 and over between 20 and 26 October.
do_this: Before you put money into an investment, pension, loan or other financial product, search for the firm on the FCA Firm Checker at fca.org.uk.
Ring or email the firm using the contact details on Firm Checker, so you know you’re dealing with the real company and not a copycat.
Seen a famous face backing an investment online? Check the firm on Firm Checker before you click or pay.
